I found no later resolution in 2 searches; this should be re-checked. Exponent convention: lambda = frequency, so lambda^{1/2} matches the original lambda^{1/4} in the eigenvalue convention.

title: Wind-driven fire confinement threshold
W: A fire spreads from a point, faster downwind: speed a + b cos(theta) in direction theta (0<=b<a). Firefighters build a barrier at speed sigma. Let sigma*(a,b) be the smallest speed that can confine the fire. Known: 1.626(a-b) <= sigma* <= 2 max (a+b cos theta) sin theta. Improve either bound, especially in the strong-wind limit b/a -> 1, where the lower bound tends to 0 but the upper bound stays near 2.6a.
M: With $F=\{r(\cos\theta,\sin\theta):0\le r\le a+b\cos\theta\}$ (convexified if $b>a/2$), $R_0=\{0\}$, and Bressan-admissible barriers ($\mathcal H^1(\gamma(t))\le\sigma t$), let $\sigma^*(a,b)$ be the infimum of the $\sigma$ that allow bounded $\bigcup_tR(t)$. Known: $\Lambda(a-b)\le\sigma^*\le2\max_{\theta}(a+b\cos\theta)\sin\theta$ with $\Lambda\approx1.6262$. Prove $\liminf_{b\to a}\sigma^*(a,b)/a>0$, or improve either bound for some fixed $b/a\in(0,1)$.
why: This is the anisotropic (wind-driven) version of Bressan's fire-confinement problem, whose isotropic threshold is still open (conjectured sigma* = 2, known only 1.626 <= sigma* <= 2). Wind is the realistic case for wildfires and makes the geometry of optimal barriers genuinely asymmetric.
notes: I derived the lower bound myself by comparison and scaling, not from the literature. I found no anisotropic necessary condition published. Grade B, not A: it derives from the famous isotropic problem, and the strong-wind regime may give way to a simple width argument.
bound: sigma*(a,b): infimum of barrier construction speeds that can confine a fire spreading with speed profile rho(theta)=a+b cos(theta)

sigma*(a,b) >= Lambda*(a-b), Lambda ~ 1.62621 (isotropic lower bound, arXiv 2610.36919, Thm 4.1). Proof: F contains the disc of radius a-b. Bressan's comparison lemma moves blocking from F to that disc, and rescaling time reduces to unit speed.

sigma*(a,b) <= 2 max_{theta in [0,pi]} (a+b cos theta) sin theta (Bressan, Thm 5, non-isotropic case; applies because rho is even and nonincreasing on [0,pi]). This equals 2a at b=0 and tends to (3 sqrt3/2) a as b->a.

title: Liouville theorem for Lane-Emden with a shifted nonlinearity
W: Gidas-Spruck: -Delta u = u^p has no positive solution on R^n for subcritical p. Replace u^p by the value of u^p at a shifted point x+e. Is there still no positive solution, for every subcritical p?
M: Let $n\ge3$, $1<p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}$, $e\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}$. Prove or disprove: there is no positive $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)$ with $-\Delta u(x)=u(x+e)^p$ for all $x$. (For $1<p<\frac n{n-2}$ the standard Mitidieri–Pohozaev test-function argument applies, since the shift is negligible at large scales; the open range is $\frac n{n-2}\le p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}$. One may also ask whether positive solutions exist for $p\ge\frac{n+2}{n-2}$.)
why: For $p<(n+2)/(n-2)$ (here $2<7/3$), Gidas–Spruck shows $-\Delta u=u^p$ has no positive entire solutions. Their proof, like moving planes, relies on the nonlinearity being local, so a shifted nonlinearity tests which Liouville methods survive nonlocal coupling.
notes: Fix: removes the arbitrary n=5,p=2 instance, states general subcritical range, and separates the easy range p<n/(n-2). No literature on shifted-argument Lane-Emden found (two searches).

title: Matching lower bound for OMv on low-VC-dimension matrices
W: Anand-van den Brand-McCarty give O~(n^2) preprocessing and O~(n^{2-1/d}) query time for Boolean Mv when M has VC-dimension d. Show, assuming OMv (or unconditionally in the cell-probe model), that n^{2-c/d} query time is necessary for some constant c, for d up to some omega(1) function; or improve the upper bound to n^{2-f(d)} with f(d) >> 1/d.
M: Lower bound: shows the OMv barrier degrades gracefully with structure, giving a quantitative 'OMv for structured inputs' hypothesis. Better upper bound: OMv hardness requires VC-dimension growing faster than believed, which would localize the hard instances.

Showing that standard prime hypotheses kill AH, or that they are compatible with it, would sharply separate what prime-side hypotheses can say about the fine structure of zeros.

title: Second moment of 3-torsion in imaginary quadratic class groups

It amounts to counting pairs of cubic fields with the same quadratic resolvent, i.e. certain degree-9 fields, which no parametrization handles. Smith's 2-primary breakthroughs do not reach odd ℓ because of the diagonal-entry problem for symmetric pairings.

title: From density to Kolmogorov typicality of positive entropy in symplectic families
W: Berger and Turaev showed that families of area-preserving surface maps having positive metric entropy at every parameter are dense among smooth families. Show this is typical, i.e. holds for a Kolmogorov-generic (prevalent) set of families, or find a robust obstruction.

Berger–Turaev (2025, Thm B) show that families with $h_{\mathrm{Leb}}(f_p)>0$ for every $p$ are dense. title: Beat the (1-o(1)) log2 d exponent in quasi-polynomial polytope diameter bounds
W: All known bounds on the diameter of a d-dimensional polyhedron with n facets have the form (n−d)^{log₂ d − O(log log d)}. The latest (Liu–Ge–Ye 2026) is (n−d)^{log₂ G_d} with G_d ~ (4 ln 2) d/(ln d)². Get an exponent at most (1−ε) log₂ d.

Known: $\Delta_u(d,n)\le (n-d)^{\log_2 G_d}$, $G_d=(4\ln2+o(1))d/(\ln d)^2$ (Liu–Ge–Ye 2026), after Kalai–Kleitman, Todd, Sukegawa. A constant-factor gain in the exponent would therefore need a structurally new argument, which is a meaningful step toward the polynomial Hirsch conjecture.
